narrative:
The 2020 Detroit Tigers entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season as a rebuilding club, and the early weeks offered genuine reason for optimism. A hot July saw the Tigers go 5-3, powered by a pair of Opening Day fireworks from Miguel Cabrera and JaCoby Jones that announced Detroit was ready to compete. A gritty August win over Cincinnati, sealed by a gift error that plated three runs, kept the Tigers afloat even as the bullpen showed troubling signs against Pittsburgh.

The middle stretch of August brought a brief flashpoint of promise — rookie Isaac Paredes announced himself with a grand slam — but the relief corps continued to crack under pressure. Matthew Boyd and Joe Jiménez surrendered critical home runs against the Pirates, and the bullpen's fragility became the defining story of Detroit's 2020. The Tigers went 11-13 in August, a respectable enough ledger on paper, but the high-leverage failures were piling up and the run differential was quietly becoming alarming.

September was where the wheels came off entirely. At 7-19, the Tigers collapsed down the stretch, and the bullpen — Gregory Soto, José Cisnero, Bryan Garcia — took the brunt of the damage. The Twins in particular feasted on Detroit's relievers across back-to-back series, and Eloy Jiménez's three-run blast off Cisnero against the White Sox encapsulated a month where the Tigers simply could not protect leads or keep games close.

In the end, the 2020 Tigers finished 23-35, a record that told the true story: a rotation ERA of 5.63 and a bullpen that repeatedly melted down in the moments that mattered most. There were flashes of what the future might hold — Paredes's grand slam, Schoop delivering clutch knocks, young arms showing life — but this was a season defined by its inability to hold games in the late innings. Detroit missed the expanded playoffs and headed into the offseason knowing the bullpen required urgent attention before this young core could truly contend.

chapters.title: Opening Fireworks
chapters.description: Miguel Cabrera and JaCoby Jones both go deep on Opening Day as the Tigers burst out of the gate with a winning July.

chapters.title: August Grind
chapters.description: Detroit grinds to a modest winning record in August, stealing games through clutch moments even as bullpen cracks begin to show.

chapters.title: Bullpen Meltdowns
chapters.description: Joe Jiménez and Matthew Boyd surrender devastating home runs against Pittsburgh, exposing the relief corps as a critical weakness.

chapters.title: A Rookie Shines
chapters.description: Isaac Paredes delivers a grand slam to provide a rare bright spot and a glimpse of Detroit's promising future.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: A 7-19 September puts the season to rest as the bullpen repeatedly surrenders leads to the Twins, White Sox, and beyond.
